match.reason: The bank point covers inventory management, holding costs and FIFO/LIFO valuation, not the cost price of inventory (purchase cost plus freight in, excluding GST) that the new point teaches.

draft.title: The cost price of inventory
card: Inventory is recorded at its cost price. This is what the business paid to buy the goods and get them ready for sale.
Costs of getting the goods ready for sale are added to the invoice price. Freight in, which is the cost of delivering the goods to the business, is one example.
GST is not part of the cost price. A business that is registered for GST can claim it back from the Australian Taxation Office, so it is not a cost to the business.
Costs after the goods are ready for sale, such as the wages of a shop assistant, are not added to the cost price of inventory.
draft.remember: Cost price is what it cost to buy the goods and get them ready for sale, without GST.

a.q: Which amount is included in the cost price of inventory?
opts: Freight in paid to deliver the goods to the shop
GST paid on the purchase of the goods
Wages paid to a person who serves customers
Advertising paid to promote the goods for sale
a.why: Freight in is a cost of getting the goods to the business so they are ready for sale. Wages for serving customers are a cost after the goods are ready, so they are not added. GST is also left out.
a.clue: Think about costs that happen before the goods can be put on the shelf.

b.q: Kiran's Cycles in Ballarat buys a bike for $600 plus $60 GST. It also pays $40 freight in, plus $4 GST. At what cost price is the bike recorded as inventory?
b.why: The cost price is $600 plus $40 freight in, which is $640. Both GST amounts are left out because the business can claim them back. $704 is wrong because it includes GST.
b.clue: Add the cost of getting the bike ready for sale, then leave out all GST.

a.best: Freight in paid to deliver the goods to the shop

problems.detail: The card says GST is left out only when a business is registered for GST, but the question never says Kiran's Cycles is registered. For an unregistered business, $704 would be the cost. Add 'which is registered for GST' to the question.
